Maintenance dose may be given orally or IV; feeding does not affect absorption
Crosses placenta; this product is for neonates - not a maternal therapy
Caffeine passes into milk; relevant when mother consumes caffeine (product is for infants)

Impaired neonatal hepatic function - use caution, monitor levels
Serum caffeine level (toxicity above 50 mg/L), heart rate, feeding tolerance, signs of NEC
summary: Caffeine citrate injection/oral solution is a methylxanthine CNS and respiratory stimulant indicated for the treatment of apnea of prematurity in preterm neonates. The recommended regimen is a loading dose of 20 mg/kg caffeine citrate IV over 30 minutes, followed by a maintenance dose of 5 mg/kg once every 24 hours (IV over 10 minutes or orally), beginning 24 hours after loading. Caffeine base is one-half the dose expressed as caffeine citrate (20 mg citrate = 10 mg base). It acts mainly by antagonizing adenosine A1 and A2 receptors, stimulating the respiratory center and the response to hypercapnia. Serum levels should be monitored (serious toxicity above 50 mg/L), and preterm infants should be watched for necrotizing enterocolitis. The neonatal half-life is very long (3-4 days) due to immature hepatic metabolism.
indications: Treatment of apnea of prematurity in preterm neonates

dosage.d: Caffeine citrate 20 mg/kg (1 mL/kg) IV over 30 minutes via syringe infusion pump - one time
Caffeine citrate 5 mg/kg (0.25 mL/kg) IV over 10 minutes or orally, every 24 hours
dosage.t: Once every 24 hours, beginning 24 hours after the loading dose

dosage.c: Prior theophylline therapy or maternal caffeine intake
dosage.d: Measure baseline serum caffeine before starting (theophylline is metabolized to caffeine in preterm infants and caffeine crosses the placenta)
Administer with caution; monitor serum caffeine concentrations and adjust dose to avoid toxicity
dosage.n: No formal PK studies in neonatal organ impairment

admin: Inspect the solution for particulate matter and discoloration before use; discard discolored or particulate-containing vials
Give the loading dose IV over 30 minutes using a syringe infusion pump
Give maintenance doses IV over 10 minutes or orally, once every 24 hours
Measure a baseline serum caffeine level if the infant received theophylline or the mother consumed caffeine before delivery
Express and verify dose carefully - caffeine base is one-half the caffeine citrate amount
moa: Caffeine is a methylxanthine structurally related to theophylline and theobromine. In apnea of prematurity its effects are attributed mainly to antagonism of adenosine A1 and A2 receptors, producing stimulation of the respiratory center, increased minute ventilation, lowered threshold to and increased response to hypercapnia, increased skeletal muscle tone, reduced diaphragmatic fatigue, and increased metabolic rate and oxygen consumption.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any component of caffeine citrate
relative: Impaired renal or hepatic function in the neonate (use caution, monitor levels)
monitor: Feeding tolerance and abdominal signs (necrotizing enterocolitis)

preg: Caffeine readily crosses the placenta. This product is intended for the preterm neonate, not as a maternal therapy. Maternal caffeine intake before delivery can raise the infant's baseline level - measure baseline serum caffeine before starting treatment.
lact: Caffeine is distributed into breast milk; this is relevant to maternal caffeine consumption rather than to administering this neonatal product. The drug here is given directly to the infant for apnea of prematurity.
renal: Pharmacokinetics in neonates with renal insufficiency have not been studied. Administer with caution, monitor serum caffeine, and adjust the dose to avoid accumulation and toxicity.
hepatic: Hepatic metabolism (CYP1A2) is immature in preterm neonates and further impaired by hepatic insufficiency. Administer with caution, monitor serum caffeine levels, and adjust the dose.

major: Theophylline - interconverts with caffeine in preterm neonates; additive toxicity, measure baseline level before switching
moderate: CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, certain macrolides) - may raise caffeine levels
CYP1A2 inducers (e.g., phenobarbital, phenytoin) - may lower caffeine levels
interactions.food: Formula feeding does not affect the time to peak concentration of oral caffeine.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause hyperglycemia, elevated BUN, and increased leukocyte count, particularly in overdose.

serious: Necrotizing enterocolitis (monitor closely; causal relationship not established)
Severe extravasation injury with peripheral IV
rare: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (single case in trial)
emergency: Seizures or marked CNS hyperexcitability with high serum levels
Signs of necrotizing enterocolitis (abdominal distention, bloody stools, lethargy)

monitoring: Serum caffeine concentration periodically (serious toxicity above 50 mg/L)
Baseline serum caffeine if prior theophylline or maternal caffeine exposure
Feeding tolerance and abdominal signs for necrotizing enterocolitis
counsel: This medicine is given to your baby to help control pauses in breathing (apnea of prematurity)
The care team will check blood levels to keep the dose safe
Report any unusual jitteriness, feeding problems, abdominal swelling or blood in the stool to the nursing team
The dose is given once a day and may be by drip or by mouth
Caffeine base is half the labeled caffeine citrate amount - the team double-checks every dose
pk: Rapid CNS distribution after dosing; therapeutic respiratory effect within hours
Oral Tmax about 30 minutes to 2 hours (caffeine base 10 mg/kg gives Cmax 6-10 mg/L)
Neonates approximately 3-4 days (immature CYP1A2); falls to about 5 hours by 9 months of age
Store at 20-25 C (controlled room temperature); protect from light; discard discolored or particulate vials
pearls: CRITICAL: caffeine base is ONE-HALF the dose expressed as caffeine citrate (20 mg citrate = 10 mg base) - dosing errors are a known hazard
Loading 20 mg/kg citrate IV over 30 min, then 5 mg/kg citrate every 24 h starting 24 h later
Neonatal half-life is 3-4 days due to immature liver - effects and toxicity are prolonged
Serious toxicity above serum 50 mg/L; monitor levels, heart rate and feeding tolerance
Watch for necrotizing enterocolitis in all treated preterm infants
missed: Dosing is managed by the neonatal care team. If a once-daily maintenance dose is missed, the team gives it when noticed and adjusts subsequent timing; doses are not doubled. Serum levels guide any adjustment.
overdose: Reported serum levels in overdose range from about 24 mg/L to 350 mg/L; serious toxicity occurs above 50 mg/L. Signs include fever, tachypnea, jitteriness, insomnia, fine tremor, hypertonia, opisthotonos, tonic-clonic movements, vomiting, hyperglycemia, raised BUN and leukocytosis; seizures, arrhythmia and heart failure can occur. There is no specific antidote - stop the drug and provide supportive care, control seizures, monitor cardiac and metabolic status; manage extravasation injury locally.
